title.zh: 卷四百〇八 列傳第一百六十七 吳昌裔 汪綱 陳宓 王霆
title.en: Volume 408 Biographies 167: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting
title.raw: 卷四百〇八 列傳第一百六十七 吳昌裔 汪綱 陳宓 王霆 Volume 408 Biographies 167: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting

sentences.zh: 吳昌裔汪綱陳宓王霆

translations.literal: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, Wang Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changyi, Wang Gang, Chen Mi, and Wang Ting.

sentences.zh: 吳昌裔，字季永，中江人。

translations.literal: Wu Changyi, style Jiyong, was a native of Zhongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changyi, whose style was Jiyong, came from Zhongjiang.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，與兄泳痛自植立，不肯逐時好，得程頤、張載、朱熹諸書，輒研繹不倦。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he and his elder brother Yong rigorously established themselves, refusing to follow the fashions of the day; obtaining the works of Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Zhu Xi, and others, he would study and interpret them without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he and his elder brother Yong strove hard to stand on their own and would not chase the tastes of the day. Once he obtained the writings of Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Zhu Xi, and the like, he studied and explicated them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年舉進士，聞漢陽守黃幹得熹之學，往從之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination; hearing that the prefect of Hanyang, Huang Gan, had received Xi's learning, he went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiading reign he passed the jinshi examination. Hearing that Huang Gan, prefect of Hanyang, had inherited Zhu Xi's learning, he went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 調閩中尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as assistant magistrate in Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant magistrate in Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 利路轉運使曹彥約聞其賢，俾司糴場。

translations.literal: The Lizhou circuit transport commissioner Cao Yanyue, hearing of his worth, had him oversee the grain-purchase depot.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue, transport commissioner of the Lizhou circuit, heard of his talent and put him in charge of the grain-purchase depot.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，議糴上流，昌裔請發本倉所儲數萬而徐糴以償，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the year was famine-stricken, and it was proposed to purchase grain upstream; Changyi requested releasing the tens of thousands stored in the local granary and gradually purchasing grain to repay it, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck that year, and officials proposed buying grain upstream. Changyi asked to release the tens of thousands of bushels held in the local granary and replenish the stock gradually through purchases; his plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 調眉州教授。

translations.literal: He was transferred to instructor at Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as instructor at Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 眉士故尚蘇軾學，昌裔取諸經為之講說，祠周惇頤及顥、頤、載、熹，揭《白鹿洞學規》，仿潭州釋奠儀，簿正祭器，士習丕變。

translations.literal: The scholars of Mei had long favored Su Shi's learning; Changyi took the classics to lecture on them, enshrined Zhou Dunyi and Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, posted the Bailudong Academy regulations, imitated the Tanzhou libation ceremony, put the sacrificial vessels in order on the register, and scholarly practice was greatly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Mei's scholars had long favored Su Shi's school of thought. Changyi lectured on the classics instead, enshrined Zhou Dunyi together with the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, posted the regulations of Bailudong Academy, modeled the Tanzhou libation rite, inventoried the sacrificial vessels, and scholarly habits changed profoundly.

sentences.zh: 製置使崔與之薦之，改知華陽縣。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Cui Yuizhi recommended him, and he was changed to magistrate of Huayang County.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Cui Yuizhi recommended him, and he was appointed magistrate of Huayang County.

sentences.zh: 修學宮，來四方士，斥羨錢二十萬緡，買良田備旱。

translations.literal: He repaired the county school, drew scholars from the four directions, expended two hundred thousand strings of surplus funds, and bought fertile fields as provision against drought.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the county school and attracted scholars from all quarters. He spent two hundred thousand strings of surplus funds to buy fertile fields as a reserve against drought.

sentences.zh: 通判眉州，著《苦言》十篇，慮蜀甚悉。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Meizhou, he composed ten chapters of Bitter Words, with very thorough concern for Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As vice-prefect of Meizhou, he wrote ten essays entitled Bitter Words, setting out his concerns for Shu in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 攝郡事，禦軍有紀律。

translations.literal: Acting in prefectural affairs, he kept the garrison troops under discipline.
translations.idiomatic: While acting prefect, he kept the garrison troops under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 尋權漢州，故事比攝官，奉饋皆如真，昌裔命削其半。

translations.literal: Soon he held acting authority over Hanzhou; by precedent, compared with acting officials, presentation gifts were all as for the real post; Changyi ordered them cut in half.
translations.idiomatic: He soon held acting authority over Han Prefecture. By custom, acting officials received presentation gifts on the same scale as regular appointees; Changyi ordered those gifts cut in half.

sentences.zh: 核兵籍，興社倉，郡政畢舉。

translations.literal: He audited the military registers, established community granaries, and prefectural administration was fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the military registers, established community granaries, and brought every item of prefectural administration to completion.

sentences.zh: 興元帥趙彥呐議東納武仙，西結秦、鞏，人莫敢言，昌裔獨奮筆力辨其非。

translations.literal: The Xingyuan commander Zhao Yan'na proposed accepting Wu Xian in the east and allying with Qin and Gong in the west; no one dared speak; Changyi alone took up his brush and vigorously argued the error.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhao Yan'na of Xingyuan proposed accepting Wu Xian in the east and allying with Qin and Gong in the west. No one else dared object, but Changyi alone took up his brush and argued forcefully that the plan was wrong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，武仙敗，二州之民果叛。

translations.literal: Before long, Wu Xian was defeated, and the people of the two prefectures indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wu Xian was defeated, and the people of the two prefectures did indeed rebel.

sentences.zh: 台臣故事，季詣獄點檢。

translations.literal: By censorial precedent, each season they went to the prisons for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: By censorial custom, each season the censors inspected the prisons.

sentences.zh: 時有爭常州田萬四千畝，平江亦數百畝，株逮百餘人，視其牘，乃趙善湘之子汝櫄、汝榟也，州縣不敢決，昌裔連疏劾罷之。

translations.literal: At the time there was a dispute over fourteen thousand mu of fields in Changzhou and several hundred mu in Pingjiang, with more than a hundred persons implicated; viewing the documents, they were the sons of Zhao Shanxiang, Rukai and Ruzi; the prefecture and county dared not decide; Changyi submitted successive memorials impeaching and removing them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a dispute involved fourteen thousand mu of fields in Changzhou and several hundred mu in Pingjiang, with more than a hundred people implicated. The papers showed that the claimants were Rukai and Ruzi, sons of Zhao Shanxiang. The local authorities dared not decide the case, so Changyi submitted a series of memorials impeaching them until they were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 冬洊雷，春大雨雪，昌裔居齋宮秉燭草疏，凡上躬缺失，宮庭嬖私，廟堂除授，皆以為言。

translations.literal: In winter thunder came repeatedly, and in spring great rain and snow fell; Changyi, dwelling in the fasting palace, held a candle and drafted memorials; whatever concerned the emperor's personal failings, palace favorites, or court appointments, he spoke on them all.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated thunder in winter and heavy rain and snow in spring moved Changyi, while residing in the fasting palace, to draft memorials by candlelight. He spoke out on every matter touching the emperor's personal failings, palace favorites, and court appointments.

sentences.zh: 又言：“將帥方命，女寵私謁，舊黨之用，邊疆之禍，皆此陰類。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Generals defying orders, female favorites making private petitions, employment of old faction members, and frontier calamities—all belong to this yin-like sort.'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Generals who defy orders, palace women who seek private favors, the revival of old factional allies, and disasters on the frontiers all spring from this same corrupting influence."

sentences.zh: ”且曰：“今大昕坐朝，間有時不視事之文；

translations.literal: And he said: 'Now at dawn the emperor sits in court, yet from time to time there are documents saying he does not attend to affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The emperor now holds court at dawn, yet from time to time edicts appear saying he is not attending to affairs;

sentences.zh: 私第謁假，或有時不入堂之報。

translations.literal: from his private residence he requests leave, or there are reports that at times he does not enter the hall.'
translations.idiomatic: from his private residence he takes leave, and there are even reports that at times he does not enter the audience hall."

sentences.zh: 上有耽樂慆逸之漸，下無協恭和衷之風。

translations.literal: Above there is the tendency to indulge in pleasure and idleness; below there is no wind of united respect and shared purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Above, the court shows a growing tendency toward indulgence and idleness; below, there is no spirit of united respect and shared purpose.

sentences.zh: 內則嬖禦懷私，為君心之蠹；

translations.literal: Within, favored attendants harbor private aims and are worms in the ruler's mind;
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, favored attendants pursue private ends and eat away at the ruler's judgment;

sentences.zh: 外則子弟寡謹，為朝政之累。

translations.literal: without, imperial kinsmen lack caution and are a burden on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: outside it, imperial kinsmen lack restraint and weigh down the conduct of government.

sentences.zh: 遊言噂遝，寵賂章聞，欲《簫》、《勺》大和，得乎？

translations.literal: Loose talk swarms, favor and bribes are openly heard—can one hope for the great harmony of the Xiao and Shao?
translations.idiomatic: Loose talk swarms everywhere, and favoritism and bribes are openly reported. How can one hope for the great harmony of the Xiao and Shao?

sentences.zh: 又念蜀事阽危，條四事以進：實規橅，審功賞，訪軍實，儲帥才。

translations.literal: He also, mindful that Shu affairs were on the brink of peril, set forth four items for presentation: make plans real, scrutinize merit rewards, investigate military realities, and store up commanders' talent.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that affairs in Shu stood on the brink of collapse, he submitted four proposals: give strategic plans real substance, scrutinize rewards for merit, investigate true military strength, and cultivate commanders' talent.

sentences.zh: 時有果、閬州守臣逃遁而進職，有知遂寧李煒父子足跡不至邊庭而受賞，僨軍之趙楷、棄城之朱揚祖皆不加罰；

translations.literal: At the time there were prefectural officials of Guo and Lang who fled yet were promoted in office; the prefect of Suining Li Wei and his son, whose footsteps never reached the frontier, yet received rewards; Zhao Kai of the mutinous army and Zhu Yangzu who abandoned the city were neither punished;
translations.idiomatic: At the time prefectural officials of Guo and Lang who had fled were nevertheless promoted, Li Wei and his son of Suining received rewards though they never set foot on the frontier, and neither Zhao Kai of the mutinous army nor Zhu Yangzu, who had abandoned his city, was punished;

sentences.zh: 又帥臣趙彥呐年老智衰，其子淫刑黷貨，士卒不用命，安癸仲恥遭抨彈，經營復用，欲起謫籍以代帥垣，昌裔皆抗疏彈擊。

translations.literal: further, the commander Zhao Yan'na was old and his wisdom decayed, his son inflicted licentious punishments and amassed illicit wealth, the soldiers would not obey orders, An Guizhong, shamed at being impeached, maneuvered for reuse, and wished to raise men from the rolls of the banished to replace the commandery—Changyi in every case submitted defiant memorials impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: moreover Commander Zhao Yan'na had grown old and feeble in judgment, his son inflicted cruel punishments and amassed illicit wealth, and the troops would not obey orders. An Guizhong, shamed by impeachment, maneuvered for reinstatement and sought to recall banished officials to replace the command structure. Changyi submitted defiant memorials attacking every one of these abuses.

sentences.zh: 又曆言三邊之事曰：“今朝廷之上，百辟晏然，言論多於施行，浮文妨於實務。

translations.literal: He also in succession spoke on the affairs of the three frontiers, saying: 'Now above the court, the hundred officials are at ease; talk exceeds execution, and floating documents obstruct practical affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke in turn on the affairs of the three frontiers: "At court today the hundred officials sit at ease. Talk outruns action, and empty documents obstruct real work."

sentences.zh: 後族王宮之冗費，列曹坐局之常程，群工閑慢之差除，諸道非泛之申請，以至土木經營，時節宴遊，神霄祈禳，大禮錫賚，藻飾治具，無異平時。

translations.literal: The redundant expenses of the empress's kin and royal palaces, the routine procedures of the various bureaus sitting at their desks, the leisurely removals of the clerical ranks, the non-routine requests of the circuits, down to construction in earth and timber, seasonal banquets and excursions, prayers at the Shenxiao Shrine, bestowals for great rites, and ornamenting the apparatus of rule—all were no different from normal times.
translations.idiomatic: The redundant expenses of the empress's kin and royal palaces, the routine paperwork of the bureaus, leisurely transfers among clerks, extraordinary requests from the circuits, construction projects, seasonal banquets and excursions, prayers at the Shenxiao Shrine, gifts for great ceremonies, and all the other trappings of governance continued as in peacetime.

sentences.zh: 至於治兵足食之方，脩車備馬之事，乃缺略不講。

translations.literal: As for methods of training troops and securing provisions, and matters of repairing chariots and preparing horses, they were omitted and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet methods for training troops and securing provisions, for repairing chariots and preparing horses, were left out entirely.

sentences.zh: ”且援靖康之敝，痛哭言之。

translations.literal: And citing the evils of the Jingkang era, he spoke with bitter weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the disasters of the Jingkang era and spoke through tears.

sentences.zh: 出為大理少卿，屢疏引去，不許。

translations.literal: He went out as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, repeatedly memorializing to withdraw, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review. He repeatedly memorialized to resign, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 會杜範再入台，擊參政李鳴復，謂昌裔與範善，必相為謀者，數讒之，以權工部侍郎出參讚四川宣撫司軍事。

translations.literal: It happened that Du Fan re-entered the Censorate and attacked the councilor Li Mingfu; saying Changyi was friendly with Fan and must be plotting together, he slandered him repeatedly, and Changyi was sent out as acting vice minister of Works to participate in and assist the military affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fan returned to the Censorate and attacked Councilor Li Mingfu, enemies said Changyi was close to Fan and must be conspiring with him. They slandered him repeatedly until he was sent out as acting vice minister of Works to participate in the military affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 人曰：“此李綱救太原也。

translations.literal: People said: 'This is Li Gang saving Taiyuan.'
translations.idiomatic: People said, "This is like Li Gang being sent to save Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 太原不可救，特以綱主戰，故出之耳。

translations.literal: Taiyuan could not be saved; he was sent out only because Gang advocated war.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan could not be saved; Li Gang was sent away only because he favored war.

sentences.zh: ”昌裔曰：“君命也，不可不亟行。

translations.literal: Changyi said: 'It is the ruler's command; one cannot but hurry to go.'
translations.idiomatic: Changyi replied, "It is the ruler's command. I must set out at once."

sentences.zh: ”慷慨襆被出關，忽得疾，中道病甚，帝聞之，授秘閣修撰，改嘉興府。

translations.literal: With high spirit he wrapped his bedding and left the pass; suddenly he fell ill, and midway his illness was severe; the emperor heard of it and appointed him Secretariat Drafter, changing him to Jiaxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He wrapped his bedding with high spirit and left the pass, but suddenly fell ill and grew gravely sick on the road. When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Changyi Secretariat Drafter and transferred him to Jiaxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昌裔曰：“吾以疾不能歸救父母，上負聖恩，下負此心，若舍遠就近，舍危就安，人其謂我何？

translations.literal: Changyi said: 'Because of illness I cannot return to rescue my parents; above I fail the sage grace, below I fail this heart—if I abandon the distant for the near and abandon peril for safety, what will people say of me?'
translations.idiomatic: Changyi said, "Illness keeps me from returning to save my parents. I fail the emperor above and my own conscience below. If I abandon the distant post for a nearby one and exchange danger for safety, what will people say of me?"

sentences.zh: ”辭至四五，而言者以避事論矣。

translations.literal: He declined four or five times, yet the critics spoke of him as shirking duty.
translations.idiomatic: He declined four or five times, yet critics accused him of shirking duty.

sentences.zh: 改贛州，辭，以右文殿修撰主管鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to Ganzhou, declined, and was made Right Culture Hall Drafter in charge of the Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ganzhou, declined again, and was made Right Culture Hall Drafter with charge of the Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提刑，辭，改知婺州。

translations.literal: He was moved to judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, declined, and was changed to prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, declined, and was appointed prefect of Wuzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 婺告旱，民日夜望之，乃不忍終辭，減騶從供帳，遣僚佐召邑令周行阡陌，蠲粟八萬一千石、錢二十五萬緡有奇。

translations.literal: Wuzhou reported drought; the people day and night looked to him; he could not bear to decline to the end; he reduced escorts and provision accounts, sent subordinates to summon county magistrates to tour the fields, and remitted eighty-one thousand shi of grain and more than two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou reported drought, and the people watched for him day and night. He could not bring himself to decline the post entirely. He cut back his escort and official expenses, sent aides to summon county magistrates for tours of the fields, and remitted eighty-one thousand shi of grain and more than two hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 加集英殿修撰，卒，以寶章閣待制致仕。

translations.literal: He was added as Hall for Assembling Excellence Drafter, died, and was made Baozhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hall for Assembling Excellence Drafter, then died and was granted retirement as Baozhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 昌裔剛正莊重，遇事敢言，典章多所閑習。

translations.literal: Changyi was upright, stern, and grave; on affairs he dared to speak; he was well versed in many regulations and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi was upright, stern, and grave, spoke boldly when matters arose, and was well versed in statutes and ritual.

sentences.zh: 嚐輯至和、紹興諸臣奏議本末。

translations.literal: He once compiled the origins and outcomes of memorial proposals by various ministers of the Zhihe and Shaoxing eras.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled the origins and outcomes of memorial proposals by ministers of the Zhihe and Shaoxing eras.

sentences.zh: 名《儲鑒》。

translations.literal: It was titled Stored Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He titled it Stored Mirror.

sentences.zh: 又會粹周、漢以至宋蜀道得失，興師取財之所，名《蜀鑒》。

translations.literal: He also gathered the gains and losses of the Shu routes from Zhou and Han down to Song, and the places where armies were raised and wealth taken, naming it Shu Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the gains and losses of the Shu routes from Zhou and Han through Song, together with the places where armies were raised and wealth exacted, and titled the work Shu Mirror.

sentences.zh: 有奏議、《四書講義》、《鄉約口義》、《諸老記聞》、《容台議禮》、文集行於世。

translations.literal: He had Memorials, Expositions on the Four Books, Oral Explications of the Village Compact, Records Heard from the Elders, Rites Discussed at the Guest Terrace, and collected writings circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Memorials, Expositions on the Four Books, Oral Explications of the Village Compact, Records Heard from the Elders, Rites Discussed at the Guest Terrace, and collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 初，昌裔與徐清叟、杜範一日並入台，皆天下正士，四方想聞風采，人至和《三諫詩》以侈之。

translations.literal: At first Changyi, together with Xu Qingsou and Du Fan, entered the Censorate on the same day; all were upright men of the realm; the four quarters longed to hear their bearing; people even composed Three Remonstrators poems to extol them.
translations.idiomatic: When Changyi entered the Censorate on the same day as Xu Qingsou and Du Fan, all three were regarded as upright men of the realm. People throughout the empire looked to their example, and some even wrote Three Remonstrators poems in praise of them.

sentences.zh: 然才七閱月以遷，故莫不惋惜雲。

translations.literal: Yet after only seven months he was transferred, so none did not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after only seven months he was transferred, and everyone regretted it.

sentences.zh: 後諡忠肅。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 汪綱，字仲舉，黟縣人，簽書樞密院勃之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Gang, style Zhongju, was a native of Yi County, great-grandson of the Secretariat Drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gang, whose style was Zhongju, came from Yi County. He was the great-grandson of Bo, who had served as Secretariat Drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以祖任入官，淳熙十四年中銓試，調鎮江府司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's yin privilege he entered office; in the fourteenth year of Chunxi he passed the selection examination and was assigned as revenue clerk of Zhenjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his grandfather's yin privilege. In the fourteenth year of the Chunxi reign he passed the selection examination and was posted as revenue clerk of Zhenjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馬大同鎮京口，強毅自任，綱言論獨不詭隨。

translations.literal: Ma Datong governed Jingkou, strong and resolute in his own course; Gang's discourse alone did not bend and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Datong governed Jingkou, he was forceful and self-willed. Gang alone refused to bend his views to suit him.

sentences.zh: 議者欲以兩淮鐵錢交子行於沿江，廷議令大同倡率行之，綱貽書曰：“邊麵行鐵錢，慮銅寶泄於外耳。

translations.literal: Those in council wished to circulate the Huai iron-cash exchange notes along the river coast; the court discussed ordering Datong to take the lead in implementing it; Gang sent a letter saying: 'On the frontier they circulate iron cash because they fear copper treasure leaking abroad.'
translations.idiomatic: Councilors wished to circulate the Huai iron-cash exchange notes along the Yangzi coast, and the court ordered Datong to take the lead. Gang wrote to him: "On the frontier they use iron cash only because they fear copper currency leaking abroad."

sentences.zh: 私鑄盛行，故錢輕而物重。

translations.literal: Private casting flourished, so money was light and goods heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Private coining is rampant, so money is debased and goods dear.

sentences.zh: 今若場務出納不以鐵錢取息，堅守四色請買舊制，冶鑄定額不求餘羨，重禁以戢私鑄，支散邊戍與在軍中半者無異，不以鐵錢準折，則淮民將自便之，何至以敝內郡邪？

translations.literal: Now if the market offices in receipts and disbursements do not take interest in iron cash, firmly uphold the old system of four-color purchase requests, fix smelting quotas without seeking surplus profit, strictly forbid to curb private casting, and disburse to frontier garrisons no differently from those half in the army, not converting by iron cash, then the Huai people will find it convenient themselves—why must we harm the inner commanderies?'
translations.idiomatic: If market offices no longer take interest in iron cash, if we firmly uphold the old four-color purchase system, fix smelting quotas without seeking surplus profit, strictly forbid private coining, and pay frontier garrisons and troops in the field on the same terms without converting through iron cash, the Huai people will manage on their own. Why should we harm the inner commanderies?"

sentences.zh: ”大同始悟。

translations.literal: Datong for the first time understood.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Datong understand.

sentences.zh: 試湖南轉運司，又中，綱笑曰：“此豈足以用世澤物耶？

translations.literal: He tested at the Hunan transport office and passed again; Gang laughed and said: 'Can this suffice to serve the age and benefit things?'
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Hunan transport office examination as well. Gang laughed and said, "Can examinations like this really serve the age or benefit the people?"

sentences.zh: ”乃刻意問學，博通古今，精究義理；

translations.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to study, broadly mastering antiquity and the present, and penetrating principle and meaning;
translations.idiomatic: He then devoted himself to learning, mastered antiquity and the present, and investigated principle and meaning deeply;

sentences.zh: 覃思本原。

translations.literal: he pondered deeply the root origin.
translations.idiomatic: pondering deeply the root of things.

sentences.zh: 調桂陽軍平陽縣令，縣連溪峒，蠻蜒與居，綱一遇以恩信。

translations.literal: He was assigned magistrate of Pingyang County in Guiyang Commandery; the county bordered stream gorges where Man and Yan peoples dwelled together; Gang at first encounter treated them with kindness and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted magistrate of Pingyang County in Guiyang Commandery, a county bordering stream gorges where Man and Yan peoples lived. From the first encounter he treated them with kindness and trust.

sentences.zh: 科罰之害既三十年，綱下車，首白諸台，罷之。

translations.literal: The harm of penal levies had already lasted thirty years; when Gang took office, he first reported to the various censorial offices and abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: Penal levies had harmed the county for thirty years. As soon as Gang took office, he reported to the censorial offices and had them abolished.

sentences.zh: 桂陽歲貢銀二萬九千餘兩，而平陽當其三分之二。

translations.literal: Guiyang annually presented more than twenty-nine thousand liang of silver in tribute, and Pingyang bore two-thirds of it.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang annually presented more than twenty-nine thousand liang of silver in tribute, of which Pingyang bore two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 綱謂向者銀礦坌發價輕，故可勉以應，今地寶已竭，市於他郡，其價倍蓰，願力請痛蠲損之。

translations.literal: Gang said that formerly silver mines had surged forth and prices were low, so one could press to meet the quota; now the land's treasure was exhausted, and buying in other commanderies doubled and redoubled the price; he wished to press earnestly for a sharp reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Gang said that formerly silver mines had flourished and prices were low, so the county could barely meet its quota. Now the local deposits were exhausted, and silver bought in other commanderies cost many times more. He pressed earnestly for a sharp reduction.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，旁邑有曹伍者，群聚惡少入境，強貸發廩，眾至千餘，挾界頭、牛橋二砦兵為援，地盤踞萬山間，前後令未嚐一涉其境，不虞綱之至也，相率出迎。

translations.literal: In a famine year, in a neighboring county there was a Cao Wu who gathered ruffians to enter the border, forcibly borrowing and opening granaries; the crowd reached more than a thousand, relying on the garrison troops of Jietou and Niuqiao forts as support; the place sat entrenched among ten thousand mountains; previous magistrates had never once entered its territory; they did not expect Gang's arrival, and came out together to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year, a man named Cao Wu in a neighboring county gathered more than a thousand ruffians who crossed the border, forced loans, and broke open granaries, backed by troops from the Jietou and Niuqiao forts in mountainous terrain no previous magistrate had ever entered. They did not expect Gang to come and went out together to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 綱已夙具酒食，令之曰：“汝何敢亂，順者得食，亂者就誅。

translations.literal: Gang had long since prepared food and drink, and ordered them: 'How dare you make disorder—those who submit will eat, those who rebel will be executed.'
translations.idiomatic: Gang had long since prepared food and drink. He ordered them: "How dare you make trouble? Those who submit will be fed; those who rebel will be executed."

sentences.zh: ”夜宿砦中，呼砦官詰責不能防守狀，皆皇恐伏地請死，杖其首惡者八人，發粟振糶，民賴以安。

translations.literal: At night he lodged in the fort, summoned the fort officers and reproached them for failing to guard, all in terror prostrating themselves begging death; he caned the eight chief villains, issued grain and sold relief grain, and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: That night he lodged in the fort, summoned the fort officers, and reproached them for failing to guard their posts. They prostrated themselves in terror and begged for death. He caned the eight ringleaders, issued grain, and sold relief grain, and the people were thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 改知金壇縣，親嫌，更弋陽縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Jintan County, but because of kinship taboo was moved to Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jintan County, but because of a kinship taboo was transferred to Yiyang County.

sentences.zh: 父義和為侍御史主管佑神觀。

translations.literal: His father Yihe was investigating censor in charge of the You Shen Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yihe served as investigating censor with charge of the You Shen Shrine.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父喪，服除，知蘭溪縣，決擿如神。

translations.literal: Soon he mourned his father's death; when mourning ended, he governed Lanxi County, deciding cases like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his father's death. When mourning ended, he governed Lanxi County and decided cases with uncanny insight.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，郡倚辦勸分，綱謂勸分所以助義倉，一切行之，非所謂安富恤貧也，願假常平錢為糶本，使得循環迭濟。

translations.literal: In a drought year the prefecture relied on organizing exhortation to share; Gang said exhortation to share was meant to assist the charity granary, and carrying it out wholesale was not what is called enriching the secure and relieving the poor; he wished to borrow Ever-Normal granary funds as capital for relief sales so they could circulate in rotation and aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year the prefecture relied on wholesale exhortation to share grain. Gang said exhortation to share was meant to support the charity granary, not to enrich the secure and relieve the poor by forcing everyone at once. He asked to borrow Ever-Normal funds as capital for relief sales so grain could circulate in rotation.

sentences.zh: 又躬勸富民浚築塘堰，大興水利，餓者得食其力，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: He also personally exhorted wealthy households to dredge and build ponds and weirs, greatly developing waterworks; the hungry could eat by their labor, and very many were wholly preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: He also personally exhorted wealthy households to dredge ponds and build weirs, greatly expanding irrigation works so the hungry could earn food by labor and very many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 郡守張抑及部使者列綱為一道荒政之冠。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked Gang the crown of famine administration in the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Yi and the circuit envoy ranked him the finest famine administrator in the circuit.

sentences.zh: 以言去，邑人相率投軌直其事，綱力止之。

translations.literal: He left because of a memorial; the townspeople in succession cast themselves before his carriage to set forth the facts straight; Gang forcefully stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: He left office after a memorial attack. The townspeople in succession cast themselves before his carriage to plead his case, but Gang firmly stopped them.

sentences.zh: 繼知太平縣，主管兩浙轉運司文字，未赴，罹內艱，擢監行在左藏西庫。

translations.literal: He next governed Taiping County and was to supervise documents of the Two-Zhe transport office but had not yet gone; he suffered inner mourning and was promoted to supervise the Western Storehouse of the Left Treasury in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He next governed Taiping County and was appointed to supervise documents for the Two-Zhe transport office, but had not yet taken up the post when he suffered the death of a close relative. He was then promoted to supervise the Western Storehouse of the Left Treasury in the capital.

sentences.zh: 屬金人殺其主允濟自立，遣使來告襲位，議者即欲遣幣，綱言：‘使名不遜，當止之境上，姑命左帑視例計辦，或且留京口總司，令盱眙諭之曰：‘紀年名節，皆犯先朝避忌，歲幣乃爾前主所增，今既易代，當復隆興、大定之舊。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jurchens killed their ruler Yunji and established themselves, sending envoys to announce succession to the throne; the councillors at once wished to send tribute; Gang said: 'The envoy's title is not deferential; he should be stopped at the border; for the moment order the Left Treasury to calculate provision by precedent, or temporarily detain him at the Jingkou general headquarters, and have Xuyi instruct him: "The reign title and tabooed names all violate our former dynasty's avoidances; the annual tribute was increased by your former ruler—now that the dynasty has changed, it should return to the Longxing and Dading precedents."'
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens killed their ruler Yunji and set up a new sovereign, they sent envoys to announce the succession and councilors at once wished to send tribute. Gang said: "The envoy's title is not deferential. He should be stopped at the border. For the moment order the Left Treasury to calculate provisions by precedent, or detain him temporarily at the Jingkou headquarters and have Xuyi instruct him: 'Your reign title and tabooed names all violate our former dynasty's avoidances, and the annual tribute was increased by your former ruler. Now that the dynasty has changed, it should return to the Longxing and Dading precedents.'"

sentences.zh: ’俟此議定，而後正旦、生辰之使可遣。

translations.literal: Wait until this matter is settled, and only then may envoys for New Year's Day and the birthday be dispatched.'
translations.idiomatic: Wait until this matter is settled, and only then may envoys for New Year's Day and the birthday be dispatched."

sentences.zh: 遲以歲月，吾擇邊將葺城堡，簡軍實，儲峙糗糧，使沿邊屹然有不可犯之勢，聽其自相攻擊，然後以全力製其後。

translations.literal: Delay for months and years; we select frontier generals to repair castles and walls, streamline military realities, store provisions and dried grain, make the border stand firm with an inviolable posture, let them attack one another, and then with full strength control them from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Delay for months and years while we choose frontier generals to repair castles, streamline military strength, and stock provisions so the border stands in an inviolable posture. Let them attack one another, and then bring full force to bear from behind.

sentences.zh: ”廟堂韙之。

translations.literal: The court approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 提轄東西庫，又幹辦諸司審計司。

translations.literal: He supervised the eastern and western storehouses, and also handled affairs for the Various Offices Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the eastern and western storehouses and also handled affairs for the Various Offices Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 以選知高郵軍，陛辭，言：“揚、楚二州當各屯二萬人，壯其聲勢，而以高郵為家計砦。

translations.literal: Through selection he became prefect of Gaoyou Commandery; at his farewell audience he said: 'Yang and Chu prefectures should each station twenty thousand men to strengthen their posture of force, and take Gaoyou as the home-base fort.'
translations.idiomatic: Selected as prefect of Gaoyou Commandery, he said at his farewell audience: "Yang and Chu prefectures should each station twenty thousand troops to strengthen their posture, with Gaoyou serving as the home-base fort."

sentences.zh: 高郵三面阻水，湖澤奧阻，戎馬所不能騁，獨西南一路直距天長，無險可守，乃去城六十里隨地經畫，或浚溝塹，或備設伏，以扼其衝。

translations.literal: Gaoyou on three sides is blocked by water; lakes and marshes are deep and obstructed, where war horses cannot gallop; only the southwest route runs straight to Tianchang with no defensible terrain; he therefore went sixty li from the city to plan according to the ground, sometimes digging ditches and moats, sometimes preparing ambushes, to choke the thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyou is blocked by water on three sides, and its lakes and marshes are too tangled for cavalry to charge freely. Only the southwest route runs straight toward Tianchang with no natural defense. He therefore went sixty li from the city to plan defenses according to the terrain, digging ditches and moats or setting ambushes to block the approach.

sentences.zh: ”又慮湖可以入淮，招水卒五千人造百艘列三砦以戒非常。

translations.literal: He also feared the lake could give access into the Huai, recruited five thousand water soldiers to build a hundred vessels arrayed in three forts to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared that the lake could give access into the Huai, so he recruited five thousand water soldiers, built a hundred vessels, and arrayed three forts to guard against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 興化民田濱海，昔範仲淹築堰以障寫鹵，守毛澤民置石達函管以疏運河水勢，歲久皆壞，綱乃增修之。

translations.literal: The fields of the people of Xinghua bordered the sea; formerly Fan Zhongyan built dikes to block the inflow of brine; the prefect Mao Zemin set stone sluice pipes to drain the transport-river current; after many years all were ruined; Gang then enlarged and repaired them.
translations.idiomatic: The farmland of Xinghua bordered the sea. Fan Zhongyan had once built dikes to block salt intrusion, and Prefect Mao Zemin had installed stone sluice pipes to drain the transport canal. After many years both works had fallen into ruin, and Gang enlarged and repaired them.

sentences.zh: 部使者聞於朝，增一秩，提舉淮東常平。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy reported to court; he was given one additional rank and made intendant of Huaidong Ever-Normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit envoy reported to court, he was given one additional rank, and he was made intendant of Huaidong Ever-Normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 淮米越江有禁，綱念“淮民有警則室廬莫保，歲凶則轉徙無歸，豐年可以少蘇，重以苛禁，自分畛域，豈為民父母意哉！

translations.literal: Huai rice crossing the river was forbidden; Gang reflected: 'When the Huai people have alarms, their houses cannot be preserved; in famine years they wander with nowhere to return; in good years they can recover a little—yet with harsh prohibitions dividing their own domains, is this the intent of parents to the people?'
translations.idiomatic: Transport of Huai rice across the Yangzi was forbidden. Gang reflected: "When alarm strikes, Huai people cannot protect their homes; in famine years they wander with nowhere to return. In good years they recover only a little, yet harsh prohibitions divide their own region. Is this how a parent to the people should act?"

sentences.zh: 請下金陵糴三十萬以通淮西之運，京口糴五十萬以通淮東之運。

translations.literal: He requested ordering Jinling to purchase three hundred thousand for passage of Huai West transport, and Jingkou to purchase five hundred thousand for passage of Huai East transport.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that Jinling purchase three hundred thousand bushels to open transport for western Huai and Jingkou purchase five hundred thousand to open transport for eastern Huai.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“兩淮之積不可多，昇、潤之積不可少。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The stores of the Two Huai cannot be too great; the stores of Sheng and Run cannot be too small.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Stores in the Two Huai cannot be too large, while stores in Sheng and Run cannot be too small."

sentences.zh: 平江積米數百萬，陳陳相因，久而紅腐，宜視其收貯近久，取餉輦下百司、諸軍。

translations.literal: Pingjiang's stored rice numbered in the millions, year piled upon year, and after long time turned red and rotten; one should look at how near or long its storage had been and take it to supply the hundred offices and various armies brought down by transport.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang's stored rice numbered in the millions, piled year upon year until it turned red and rotten. He proposed examining how long each store had been held and using the oldest grain to supply the capital offices and armies.

sentences.zh: 江上歲餫當至京者，貯之京口、金陵轉漕。

translations.literal: The annual grain transport on the river that should reach the capital should be stored at Jingkou and Jinling for relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Annual grain transport on the Yangzi bound for the capital should be stored at Jingkou and Jinling for relay shipment.

sentences.zh: 兩淮、中都諸倉，亦當廣糴以補其數。

translations.literal: The various granaries of the Two Huai and the central capital region should also broadly purchase grain to supplement their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries in the Two Huai and the central capital region should also purchase grain broadly to replenish their stocks.

sentences.zh: 製置使訪綱備禦孰宜先，綱言：“淮地自昔號財賦淵藪，西有鐵冶，東富魚稻，足以自給。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner asked Gang which defense preparations should come first; Gang said: 'The Huai region from old was called a deep source of revenue; in the west there is iron smelting, in the east rich in fish and rice—sufficient for self-supply.'
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commissioner asked which defensive preparations should come first. Gang said: "The Huai region has long been called a deep treasury of revenue. Ironworks lie to the west and fish and rice abound to the east, enough for self-sufficiency."

sentences.zh: 淮右多山，淮左多水，足以自固。

translations.literal: Huai West has many mountains, Huai East much water—enough for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Western Huai has many mountains and eastern Huai much water, enough for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 誠能合兩淮為一家，兵財通融，聲勢合一，雖不假江、浙之力可也。

translations.literal: If truly the Two Huai could be united as one household, with troops and wealth flowing together and posture of force made one, even without borrowing the strength of Jiang and Zhe it could suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If the Two Huai could truly be united as one, with troops and wealth flowing together and their combined posture made one, they could suffice even without relying on Jiang and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 祖宗盛時，邊郡所儲足支十年；

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of the ancestors, what the border commanderies stored sufficed to support ten years;
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's flourishing age, border commanderies stored enough grain to last ten years;

sentences.zh: 慶曆間，中山一鎮尚百八十萬石。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era, one garrison of Zhongshan still had 1.8 million shi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era, a single garrison in Zhongshan still held 1.8 million shi.

sentences.zh: 今宜上法先朝，令商旅入粟近塞，而算請錢貨於京師。

translations.literal: Now one should take the high law of the former court, order merchants and travelers to bring grain into the vicinity of the passes, and calculate requests for money and goods in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court should now follow the former dynasty's precedent, allow merchants to deliver grain near the frontier passes, and issue capital vouchers redeemable in the capital.

sentences.zh: 入粟拜爵，守之以信，則輸者必多，邊儲不患不豐。

translations.literal: For bringing grain one receives ennoblement; if this is kept with trust, then those who deliver will surely be many, and border stores need not fear lacking abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who delivered grain received ennoblement, and if the promise were kept faithfully, deliveries would multiply and border stores would never lack for grain.

sentences.zh: 州郡禁兵本非供役，乃就糧外郡耳，今不為戰鬥用，乃使之共力役，緩急戍守，專倚大軍，指日待更，不安風土，豈若土兵生長邊地，墳墓室家，人自為守邪？

translations.literal: The forbidden troops of prefectures and commanderies were originally not for supplying labor but for drawing rations in outer commanderies; now they are not used for fighting but made to share in labor service; in urgency or ease for garrison defense they rely solely on the great army, counting days awaiting rotation, ill at ease in the local climate—how can this compare to local troops growing up on the border, with graves and households, each man guarding for himself?
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural forbidden troops were never meant for corvée labor but to draw rations in outer commanderies. Now they are not used for battle but forced into labor service. In emergencies the frontier relies solely on the main army, whose men count the days until rotation and never settle into local conditions. How can that compare with local troops who grew up on the border, with graves and families there, and guard the land as their own?

sentences.zh: 當精擇伉壯，廣其尺籍，悉隸御前軍額，分擘券給以助州郡衣糧之供，大率如山陽武鋒軍製，則邊麵不必抽江上之戍，江上不必出禁闈之師。

translations.literal: One should carefully select the strong and robust, broaden their registers, attach them all to the Imperial Front Army rolls, divide and issue certificates to assist prefectures and commanderies in clothing and grain supply, generally following the Shanyang Martial Vanguard system—then the frontier need not draw garrisons from the river, and the river need not send out troops from the forbidden inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The court should carefully select strong men, expand their registers, attach them all to Imperial Front Army rolls, and issue ration certificates to help prefectures supply clothing and grain, generally following the Shanyang Martial Vanguard system. Then the frontier need not draw garrisons from the Yangzi, and the Yangzi need not send palace troops.

sentences.zh: 生券更番，勞費俱息。

translations.literal: With living certificates and rotating shifts, labor and expense would both cease.
translations.idiomatic: With living certificates and rotating shifts, both labor and expense would cease.

sentences.zh: 時有獻言製司廣買荒田開墾，以為營田，綱以為“荒瘠之地不難辦，而工力、水利非久不可，棄產欺官，良田終不可得，耗費公帑，開墾難就。

translations.literal: At the time someone proposed to the Pacification Commission broadly buying waste land for opening and cultivation as military farms; Gang considered that 'waste and barren land is not hard to arrange, but labor and waterworks cannot be done in a short time; abandoning property and deceiving the government, good fields in the end cannot be obtained, public funds are wasted, and opening cultivation is hard to accomplish.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone then proposed that the Pacification Commission buy waste land broadly for military farms. Gang argued: "Waste land is easy to acquire, but labor and waterworks cannot be completed quickly. People abandon property, deceive officials, and good fields never materialize. Public funds are wasted and cultivation rarely succeeds."

sentences.zh: 曷若勸民盡耕閑田，川澮堙塞則官為之助，變瘠為沃，使民有餘蓄。

translations.literal: How much better to exhort the people to fully cultivate idle fields; when streams and canals are blocked, let the government assist; change barren into fertile, and let the people have surplus stores.
translations.idiomatic: Far better to urge the people to cultivate idle fields fully, have the government assist when streams and canals are blocked, turn barren soil fertile, and let the people build surplus stores.

sentences.zh: 晁錯入粟之議，本朝便糴之法，在其中矣。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo's proposal for bringing in grain and this dynasty's convenient-purchase method are contained within this.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo's proposal for grain deliveries and this dynasty's convenient-purchase system already embody this approach.

sentences.zh: ”製司知其無益，乃止。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commission knew it was without benefit and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commission saw that the plan was useless and dropped it.

sentences.zh: 淮東煮鹽之利，本居天下半，歲久敝滋，鹽本日侵，帑儲空竭，負兩總司五十餘萬，亭戶二十八萬，借撥於朝廷五十萬，又會餉所復鹽鈔，舊制弗許商人預供貼鈔錢，鹽司坐是窘不能支。

translations.literal: The profit of Huaidong's salt boiling originally comprised half the realm; over years decay increased, the salt capital daily eroded, treasury stores were emptied, owing the two general offices more than five hundred thousand, the saltern households two hundred eighty thousand, borrowed from court five hundred thousand, and again the ration office restored salt notes; the old system did not permit merchants to advance payment for note subsidies; the salt office sat in distress unable to support itself.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidong's salt-boiling profits had once comprised half the empire's revenue, but over the years decay spread, salt capital eroded daily, and treasury stores emptied. The office owed the two general commissions more than five hundred thousand strings, owed saltern households two hundred eighty thousand, and had borrowed five hundred thousand from court. When the ration office restored salt notes, the old rule forbade merchants to advance subsidy payments, leaving the salt office unable to support itself.

sentences.zh: 綱抉擿隱伏，凡虛額無實，詭為出內，飛走移易，事製曲防，課乃更羨。

translations.literal: Gang probed and exposed what was hidden; whatever had empty quotas without reality, falsely presented as disbursement, flown and shifted and exchanged, matters bent and guarded against—then the levy became surplus instead.
translations.idiomatic: Gang exposed hidden abuses: empty quotas, false disbursements, and shifting accounts. Once these practices were blocked, revenue actually increased.

sentences.zh: 既盡償所負，又贏金三十萬緡，為樁辦庫，以備鹽本之闕。

translations.literal: Having fully repaid what was owed, he also gained three hundred thousand strings in gold, established a reserve treasury, and prepared against shortfalls in salt capital.
translations.idiomatic: After repaying all debts, he still gained three hundred thousand strings, established a reserve treasury, and prepared against shortfalls in salt capital.

sentences.zh: 添置新灶五十所，諸場悉視乾道舊額三百九十萬石，通一千三百萬緡，課官吏之殿最。

translations.literal: He added fifty new salterns; all depots were made to meet the Qiandao old quota of 3.9 million shi, totaling 13 million strings, and officials' performance was ranked.
translations.idiomatic: He added fifty new salterns, required all depots to meet the Qiandao quota of 3.9 million shi totaling thirteen million strings in revenue, and ranked officials by performance.

sentences.zh: 綱約己率下，辭台郡之互饋，獨增場官奉以養其廉。

translations.literal: Gang restrained himself and led those below; he declined mutual gifts between censorial and prefectural offices, and alone increased depot officials' salaries to nurture their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gang restrained himself and led subordinates by example. He declined mutual gifts between censorial and prefectural offices and alone increased depot officials' salaries to support their integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部員外郎、總領淮東軍馬財賦。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and overall director of Huaidong military horses and fiscal levies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and overall director of Huaidong military horses and fiscal levies.

sentences.zh: 時邊麵多生券，山東歸附月餉錢糧，以緡計增三十有三萬，米以石計增六萬，真、楚諸州又新招萬弩手，皆仰給總所，而浙西鹽利積負至七十餘萬緡，諸州漕運不以時至。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier mostly had living certificates; Shandong submission monthly rations in money and grain increased by three hundred thirty thousand strings and sixty thousand shi; Zhen and Chu commanderies newly recruited ten thousand crossbowmen—all relied on the general office for supply, while western Zhe salt profits accumulated deficits reaching more than seven hundred thousand strings, and various prefectures' transport grain did not arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the frontier relied heavily on living certificates. Monthly rations for Shandong submissions rose by three hundred thirty thousand strings and sixty thousand shi of grain. Zhen and Chu commanderies newly recruited ten thousand crossbowmen, all dependent on the general office. Meanwhile western Zhe salt profits ran a deficit of more than seven hundred thousand strings, and transport grain from various prefectures failed to arrive on schedule.

sentences.zh: 綱核名實，警稽慢，區畫處分，餉事賴以不乏。

translations.literal: Gang verified names against realities, warned against delay in audit, planned and disposed matters, and ration affairs relied on this to avoid shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Gang verified accounts against reality, warned against delays in audit, planned and disposed affairs, and thereby kept rations from running short.

sentences.zh: 移疾乞閑，得直秘閣、知婺州，改提點浙東刑獄，皆屢辭不得請。

translations.literal: He reported illness and begged leisure, obtaining Secretariat Drafter and prefect of Wuzhou; he was changed to judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang—all repeatedly declined but requests were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported illness and asked for a quieter post, receiving appointment as Secretariat Drafter and prefect of Wuzhou, then transfer as judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang. He declined repeatedly but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 慮囚，至婺，有奴挾刃欲戕其主，不遇而殺其子，瞞讕妄牽連，徑出斬之。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners, upon reaching Wuzhou, there was a slave who seized a blade wishing to kill his master; failing to meet him, he killed the master's son; falsely implicating others in deception, Gang directly ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in Wuzhou, he found a slave who had seized a blade to kill his master, failed to find him, and killed the master's son instead, then falsely implicated others. Gang ordered him executed at once.

sentences.zh: 釋衢囚之冤者。

translations.literal: He released those wrongly imprisoned in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He released prisoners wrongly held in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 台盜鍾百一非共盜，尉覬賞，躐申製司，綱謂：“治盜雖尚嚴，豈得鍛煉傅會以成其罪邪？

translations.literal: In Taizhou the thief Zhong Baiyi was not a co-thief; the assistant magistrate coveted reward and leaped to report to the Pacification Commission; Gang said: 'Though punishing thieves values severity, how can one forge and join charges to complete the crime?'
translations.idiomatic: In Taizhou a thief named Zhong Baiyi was not a co-conspirator, but the assistant magistrate, coveting a reward, rushed the case to the Pacification Commission. Gang said, "Thieves must be punished severely, but how can charges be forged to complete a case?"

sentences.zh: ”於是得減死。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sentence was reduced from death.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was therefore reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 禱雨龍瑞宮，有物蜿蜒朱色，盤旋壇上者三日。

translations.literal: Praying for rain at Longrui Palace, there was a thing winding in vermilion color, coiling on the altar terrace for three days.
translations.idiomatic: While praying for rain at Longrui Palace, a vermilion creature wound about the altar terrace for three days.

sentences.zh: 綱曰：“吾欲雨而已，毋為異以惑眾。

translations.literal: Gang said: 'I only want rain; do not make wonders to confuse the crowd.'
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "I want only rain. Do not make wonders to confuse the people."

sentences.zh: ”言未竟，雷雨大至，歲以大熟。

translations.literal: Before his words were finished, great thunder and rain arrived, and the year had a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, thunder and heavy rain arrived, and the year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 進直煥章閣、知紹興府、主管浙東安撫司公事兼提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He advanced to direct attendant of the Hall of Glorious Culture, prefect of Shaoxing, and supervisor of eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission affairs while also serving as judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted direct attendant of the Hall of Glorious Culture, appointed prefect of Shaoxing, and made supervisor of eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission affairs while also serving as judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 訪民瘼，罷行尤切。

translations.literal: Inquiring into the people's afflictions, he abolished practices with especial urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring into the people's hardships, he abolished abusive practices with especial urgency.

sentences.zh: 蕭山有古運河，西通錢塘，東達台、明，沙漲三十餘里，舟行則膠。

translations.literal: Xiaoshan had an ancient transport canal, west connecting to Qiantang, east reaching Tai and Ming; sand rose for more than thirty li, and boats when traveling stuck fast.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshan had an ancient transport canal running west to Qiantang and east to Tai and Ming. Sand had built up for more than thirty li, trapping boats in place.

sentences.zh: 乃開浚八千餘丈，復創閘江口，使泥淤弗得入，河水不得泄，於塗則盡甃以達城。

translations.literal: He then dredged more than eight thousand zhang, restored the sluice at the river mouth so mud and silt could not enter and river water could not spill out, and along the road fully paved with brick to reach the city.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged more than eight thousand zhang, restored the sluice at the river mouth to keep silt out and control the current, and paved the towpath with brick all the way to the city.

sentences.zh: 十里創一廬。

translations.literal: Every ten li he created one lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten li he built a rest lodge.

sentences.zh: 名曰“施水 ”，主以道流。

translations.literal: They were named 'Bestowing Water,' managed by Daoist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: He named them "Bestowing Water" and placed them under Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 於是舟車水陸，不問晝夜暑寒，意行利涉，歡欣忘勩。

translations.literal: Thereupon by boat and cart, water and land, regardless of day or night, heat or cold, travelers went as they wished with easy passage, rejoicing and forgetting fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter travelers by boat and cart, on water and land, passed day or night, in heat or cold, with easy passage and rejoicing that forgot fatigue.

sentences.zh: 屬邑諸縣瀕海，而諸暨十六鄉瀕湖，蕩濼灌溉之利甚博，勢家巨室率私植埂岸，圍以成田，湖流既束，水不得去，雨稍多則溢入邑居，田閭浸蕩。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties all bordered the sea, while Zhuji's sixteen townships bordered the lake; the benefit of marsh irrigation was very broad; powerful families and great houses mostly privately planted embankments and dikes, enclosing them to form fields; once lake flow was bound, water could not leave; when rain was slightly heavy it overflowed into towns and dwellings, and fields and hamlets were inundated.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties bordered the sea, while sixteen townships of Zhuji bordered the lake, where marsh irrigation brought broad benefit. Powerful families privately built embankments and enclosed lake margins as fields. Once the lake flow was choked, water could not drain away, and even moderate rain flooded towns and farmland.

sentences.zh: 瀕海藉塘為固，堤岸易圮，鹹鹵害稼，歲損動數十萬畝，蠲租亦萬計。

translations.literal: Bordering the sea they relied on ponds for solidity; dikes and banks easily collapsed; brine harmed the crops; yearly losses often reached hundreds of thousands of mu; rent remissions also numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal fields relied on ponds for protection, but dikes easily collapsed and brine ruined crops. Losses often reached hundreds of thousands of mu yearly, with rent remissions numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 以綱言，詔提舉常平司發田園，奇援巧請，一切峻卻，而湖田始復；

translations.literal: Following Gang's words, an edict ordered the Ever-Normal intendant to expose field estates; strange pleas and clever requests were all sternly rejected, and lake fields began to be restored;
translations.idiomatic: On Gang's recommendation, an edict ordered the Ever-Normal intendant to expose encroached estates. Strange pleas and clever requests were all sternly rejected, and lake fields began to be restored;

sentences.zh: 郡備緡錢三萬專備修築，而海田始固。

translations.literal: the prefecture prepared thirty thousand strings specially for repair and construction, and coastal fields began to be secured.
translations.idiomatic: the prefecture set aside thirty thousand strings specifically for repairs, and coastal fields began to be secured.

sentences.zh: 綱謂：“是邦控臨海道，密拱都畿，而軍籍單弱。

translations.literal: Gang said: 'This commandery controls the coastal route and closely guards the capital region, yet military registers are thin and weak.'
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "This commandery commands the coastal route and closely guards the capital region, yet its military registers are thin and weak."

sentences.zh: ”乃招水軍，刺叉手，教習甚專，不令他役。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited water troops, branded fork-handlers, trained them with great focus, and did not assign other duties.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore recruited water troops, branded fork-handlers, trained them intensively, and assigned them no other duties.

sentences.zh: 創營千餘間，寬整堅密，增置甲兵，威聲赫然。

translations.literal: He created more than a thousand barracks, broad, orderly, solid, and tight; added armor and weapons; and his martial renown blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: He built more than a thousand barracks, broad, orderly, and solid, added armor and weapons, and his martial renown blazed forth.

sentences.zh: 兼權司農卿，尋直龍圖閣，因任。

translations.literal: He concurrently held acting Minister of Agriculture, soon became direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as acting Minister of Agriculture, soon became direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，詔為右文殿修撰，加集英殿修撰，復因任，又加寶謨閣待制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was ordered Right Culture Hall Drafter, added Hall for Assembling Excellence Drafter, again continued in office, and further made Baomo Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, Gang was appointed Right Culture Hall Drafter, then Hall for Assembling Excellence Drafter, continued in office, and was further made Baomo Pavilion Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 寶慶三年大水，綱發粟三萬八千餘、緡錢五萬振之，蠲租六萬餘石，捐瘠頓蘇，無異常歲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing great flood came; Gang issued more than thirty-eight thousand shi of grain and fifty thousand strings to relieve it, remitted more than sixty thousand shi of rent, and the emaciated suddenly revived, no different from a normal year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoqing a great flood struck. Gang issued more than thirty-eight thousand shi of grain and fifty thousand strings for relief, remitted more than sixty thousand shi of rent, and the starving revived as if it were a normal year.

sentences.zh: 越有經總製窠名四十一萬，其中二十五，則紹興以來虛額也，前後帥懼負殿，以修奉欑宮之資偽增焉。

translations.literal: Yue had general-fund account names totaling four hundred ten thousand, of which two hundred fifty thousand were empty quotas since Shaoxing; successive commanders feared failing their quotas and falsely inflated them with funds for repairing and supplying the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had general-fund account entries totaling four hundred ten thousand strings, of which two hundred fifty thousand were empty quotas since the Shaoxing era. Successive commanders, fearing shortfalls, had falsely inflated them with funds earmarked for repairing the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 綱謂：“負殿之責小，罔上之罪大”。

translations.literal: Gang said: 'The blame for failing quotas is small; the crime of deceiving one's superiors is great.'
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Failing a quota is a small fault; deceiving one's superiors is a great crime."

sentences.zh: 摭其實以聞。

translations.literal: He gathered the facts and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the facts and reported them to court.

sentences.zh: 詔免九萬五千緡，而宿敝因是著明矣。

translations.literal: An edict remitted ninety-five thousand strings, and long-standing abuses thereby became clearly known.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted ninety-five thousand strings, and long-standing abuses thereby became clearly exposed.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，召赴行在，綱入見，言：“臣下先利之心過於徇義，為身之計過於謀國，俞惰退縮，奔競貪黷，相與為欺，宜有以轉移之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was summoned to the traveling court; Gang entered audience and said: 'Subjects' hearts putting profit first exceed adhering to righteousness; plans for oneself exceed planning for the state; they are compliant, lazy, retreating, and shrinking, rushing in competition, greedy and corrupt, deceiving one another together—there should be means to shift this.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding he was summoned to the traveling court. At audience Gang said, "Officials now put profit before righteousness and personal plans before the state. They are compliant, lazy, and shrinking, rush in competition, grow greedy and corrupt, and deceive one another. The court should find means to shift this."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“聞卿治行甚美，越中民力如何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I have heard your governance and conduct are very fine—how is the people's strength in central Yue?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have heard your governance is excellent. How are the people's resources in central Yue?"

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“ 去歲水潦，諸暨為甚，今歲幸中熟，十年之間，千里晏安，皆朝廷威德所及，臣何力之有。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Last year there was flood; Zhuji suffered most severely; this year we are fortunate to have a middling harvest; within ten years a thousand li are peaceful—all reach of the court's august virtue; what strength have I?'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Last year's floods hit Zhuji hardest. This year we are fortunate to have a fair harvest. Within ten years a thousand li have been peaceful, all through the court's august virtue. What strength have I?"

sentences.zh: ”權戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made acting vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 越數月，上章致仕，特畀二秩，守戶部侍郎，仍賜金帶。

translations.literal: After several months he submitted a memorial to retire; he was specially granted two ranks, retained as vice minister of Revenue, and still bestowed a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he memorialized to retire. He was specially granted two ranks, retained as vice minister of Revenue, and bestowed a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 卒，越人聞之多墮淚，有相率哭於寺觀者。

translations.literal: He died; when the people of Yue heard, many shed tears, and some went together to weep at temples and shrines.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, many people of Yue shed tears, and some went together to weep at temples and shrines.

sentences.zh: 綱學有本原，多聞博記，兵農、醫卜、陰陽、律曆諸書，靡不研究；

translations.literal: Gang's learning had root and origin; he broadly heard and broadly remembered; books on military affairs, agriculture, medicine, divination, yin-yang, pitch pipes, and calendars—none did he not investigate;
translations.idiomatic: Gang's learning had deep roots. He was widely informed and remembered much. He investigated books on military affairs, agriculture, medicine, divination, yin-yang, pitch pipes, and calendars;

sentences.zh: 機神明銳，遇事立決。

translations.literal: his mind was spirit-like and sharp, and on affairs he decided at once.
translations.idiomatic: his mind was sharp and spirit-like, and he decided affairs at once.

sentences.zh: 在越佩四印，文書山積，而能操約禦詳，治事不過二十刻，公庭如水。

translations.literal: In Yue he wore four seals; documents piled like mountains, yet he could hold to brevity and control detail; handling affairs took no more than twenty quarters of an hour; the public hall was like water.
translations.idiomatic: In Yue he bore four seals and faced documents piled like mountains, yet he held to brevity while mastering detail, finished business in no more than twenty quarters of an hour, and kept the public hall as calm as still water.

sentences.zh: 卑官下吏，一言中理，慨然從之。

translations.literal: For low officials and subordinate clerks, if one word hit the principle, he would follow it with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: If a low official or clerk spoke one word that hit the principle, he would follow it wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 為文尤長於論事，援據古今，辨博雄勁。

translations.literal: In writing he was especially skilled at discussing affairs, citing antiquity and the present, argumentative, broad, and powerfully vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he excelled at discussing affairs, citing antiquity and the present in arguments that were broad, forceful, and vigorous.

sentences.zh: 服用不喜奢麗，供帳車剩，雖敝不更。

translations.literal: In dress and use he did not like luxury; provision accounts and carriage fittings, though worn, he would not replace.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked luxury in dress and furnishings. Provision accounts and carriage fittings, though worn, he would not replace.

sentences.zh: 所著有《恕齋集》、《左帑志》、《漫存錄》。

translations.literal: His writings included Collected Works of the Forgiving Studio, Records of the Left Treasury, and Casual Preserved Notes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Collected Works of the Forgiving Studio, Records of the Left Treasury, and Casual Preserved Notes.

sentences.zh: 陳宓，字師復，丞相俊卿之子。

translations.literal: Chen Mi, style Shifu, was the son of Chief Councilor Junqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mi, whose style was Shifu, was the son of Chief Councilor Junqing.

sentences.zh: 少嚐及登朱熹之門，熹器異之。

translations.literal: In youth he once reached and entered Zhu Xi's gate; Xi regarded him as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered Zhu Xi's school, and Zhu Xi regarded him as exceptional.

sentences.zh: 長從黃幹遊。

translations.literal: When grown he followed Huang Gan in study.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied under Huang Gan.

sentences.zh: 以父任曆泉州南安鹽稅，主管南外睦宗院、再主管西外，知安溪縣。

translations.literal: Through his father's yin privilege he successively served as Nan'an salt tax officer in Quanzhou, supervised the Southern Outer Muzong Court, again supervised the Western Outer Court, and governed Anxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's yin privilege he served as Nan'an salt tax officer in Quanzhou, supervised the Southern Outer Muzong Court and then the Western Outer Court, and governed Anxi County.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，入監進奏院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he entered service as supervisor of the Memorial Submission Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiading he entered service as supervisor of the Memorial Submission Court.

sentences.zh: 時無敢慷慨盡言者，宓上封事言：“宮中宴飲或至無節，非時賜予為數浩穰，一人蔬食而嬪禦不廢於擊鮮，邊事方殷而樁積反資於妄用，此宮闈儀刑有未正也。

translations.literal: At the time none dared speak generously to the full; Mi submitted a sealed memorial saying: 'Palace banquets and drinking sometimes reach lack of restraint; untimely bestowals are numerous and vast; one man eats vegetables while consorts and attendants do not cease striking fresh meat; frontier affairs are just pressing while piled stores instead fund reckless use—this is that palace ritual and discipline are not yet corrected.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time none dared speak boldly. Mi submitted a sealed memorial: "Palace banquets sometimes know no restraint, untimely gifts are lavish, the emperor eats plainly while consorts still feast on fresh meat, and frontier affairs are pressing while piled stores fund reckless spending. Palace ritual and discipline are not yet corrected."

sentences.zh: 大臣所用非親即故，執政擇易製之人，台諫用慎默之士，都司樞掾，無非親昵，貪吏靡不得誌，廉士動招怨尤，此朝廷權柄有所分也。

translations.literal: Great ministers employ none who are not kin or old associates; the councilors choose men easy to control; the censors choose cautious and silent gentlemen; bureau and privy clerks are all without exception intimate favorites; corrupt officials none fail to get their will; upright men constantly invite resentment—this is that court authority is divided.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers employ only kin or old associates, councilors choose men easy to control, censors choose the cautious and silent, and bureau and privy clerks are all intimate favorites. Corrupt officials always get their way while upright men invite resentment. Court authority is divided."

sentences.zh: 鈔鹽變易，楮幣秤提，安邊所創立，固執己見，動失人心，敗軍之將躐躋殿岩，庸鄙之夫久尹京兆，宿將有守成之功，以小過而貶，三牙無汗馬之勞，托公勤而擢，此政令刑賞多所舛逆也。

translations.literal: Salt notes change, paper currency is weighed and raised, frontier pacification offices are newly established, they cling to their own views and constantly lose popular hearts; defeated generals leap over ranks to the palace steps, vulgar and base men long govern the capital, veteran generals with achievements in holding what was won are demoted for small faults, the Three Yamen without sweat-horse merit are promoted under plea of public diligence—this is that government orders, punishments, and rewards mostly run contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Salt notes change, paper currency is manipulated, frontier offices cling to their own views and lose popular support, defeated generals leap to high office, vulgar men long govern the capital, veteran generals with real achievements are demoted for small faults, and the Three Yamen are promoted without merit under plea of diligence. Government orders, punishments, and rewards mostly run contrary."

sentences.zh: 若能交飭內外，一正紀綱，天且不雨，臣請伏麵謾之罪。

translations.literal: If we can mutually admonish within and without and unify correction of discipline, and Heaven still does not rain, your subject requests to submit to the crime of lying face down in noodles.
translations.idiomatic: If the court can admonish within and without and unify discipline, and Heaven still withholds rain, I ask to submit to the crime of lying face down in noodles."

sentences.zh: ”奏入，丞相史彌遠不樂，而中宮慶壽，三牙獻遺，至是為之罷卻。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was displeased, but the inner palace celebration of longevity and the Three Yamen's presentation gifts were on that account halted and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was displeased, but the inner palace longevity celebration and the Three Yamen's presentation gifts were halted on that account.

sentences.zh: 尋遷軍器監簿。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to registrar of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to registrar of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉對言：

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at audience rotation he spoke:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at audience rotation he spoke:

sentences.zh: 人主之德貴乎明，大臣之心貴乎公，台諫之言貴乎直。

translations.literal: The ruler's virtue values clarity above all; the great ministers' hearts value fairness above all; the censors' words value directness above all.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's virtue values clarity above all, great ministers' hearts value fairness above all, and censors' words value directness above all.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨政雖勤而治功未舉，奉身雖儉而財用未豐，愛民雖仁而實惠未遍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty governs diligently yet governing achievement is not raised; you are personally frugal yet finances are not abundant; you love the people benevolently yet real benefit is not widespread.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs diligently yet achievement is not realized, lives frugally yet finances are not abundant, and loves the people benevolently yet real benefit does not reach them widely.

sentences.zh: 良由上下相蒙，務於欺蔽。

translations.literal: This truly comes from above and below deceiving one another, devoted to concealment.
translations.idiomatic: This truly comes from above and below deceiving one another and devoted to concealment.

sentences.zh: 匭奏囊封，有懷畢吐，陛下付近臣差擇，是有意於行其言也。

translations.literal: Box memorials and sealed pouches let those with feelings speak fully; Your Majesty entrusts nearby ministers to select and differentiate—this shows intent to carry out their words.
translations.idiomatic: Box memorials and sealed pouches let those with grievances speak fully, and Your Majesty entrusts nearby ministers to select among them, showing intent to act on their words.

sentences.zh: 而有司惟取專攻上躬與移咎牧守之章，騰播中外，以答觀聽。

translations.literal: Yet the offices only take chapters specializing in attacking the emperor's person and shifting blame to prefects and commanders, spreading them within and without to answer what is seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the offices only take memorials attacking the emperor's person or shifting blame to prefects and commanders, spread them throughout the realm, and call that a response.

sentences.zh: 今赤地千里，蝗飛蔽天，如此其可畏，猶或諱晦以旱不為災、蝗不害稼，其他誣罔，抑又可知。

translations.literal: Now red earth stretches a thousand li, locusts fly blotting out the sky—so fearsome is it—yet some still conceal and obscure, saying drought is not disaster and locusts do not harm crops; other falsehoods and deceptions may likewise be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now red earth stretches a thousand li and locusts blot out the sky. Yet some still conceal the truth, saying drought is no disaster and locusts harm no crops. Other deceptions may likewise be imagined.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰人主之德貴乎明。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says the ruler's virtue values clarity above all.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say the ruler's virtue values clarity above all.

sentences.zh: 大臣施設，浸異厥初。

translations.literal: The great ministers' arrangements gradually differ from their beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers' conduct gradually diverges from their beginnings.

sentences.zh: 凡建議求言之人，則以他事逐，諫官言事稍直，則以他職徙。

translations.literal: Whoever proposed seeking words is driven off on other grounds; remonstrance officials whose words are slightly direct are transferred to other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever proposed seeking candid speech is driven off on other grounds; remonstrance officials who speak even slightly directly are transferred to other posts.

sentences.zh: 忠憤者指為不靖，切直者目曰沽名，眾怨所萃則相繼超升，物論所歸則以次疏外。

translations.literal: The loyal and indignant are pointed to as unrestful; the cutting and direct are eyed as fishing for name; those whom popular resentment gathers are in succession promoted above rank; those whom public opinion favors are in order relegated outward.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and indignant are called unrestful, the cutting and direct are eyed as fishing for fame, those whom popular resentment gathers are promoted in succession, and those whom public opinion favors are relegated outward in turn.

sentences.zh: 某人之遷，是嚐重人罪以快同列之私忿者；

translations.literal: A certain man's transfer was one who once aggravated others' crimes to satisfy colleagues' private resentment;
translations.idiomatic: A certain man's transfer was of one who once aggravated others' crimes to satisfy colleagues' private resentment;

sentences.zh: 某人之擢，是嚐援古事以文邇日之天變者。

translations.literal: a certain man's promotion was one who once cited ancient affairs to ornament recent heaven's changes.
translations.idiomatic: a certain man's promotion was of one who once cited ancient affairs to ornament recent heaven-sent omens.

sentences.zh: 直節重望以私嫌而久棄，老奸宿臧以巧請而牽復。

translations.literal: Upright integrity and heavy reputation are long cast aside over private dislike; old villains and long-standing evildoers are drawn back through clever pleas.
