translations.idiomatic: Upright men of heavy reputation are long cast aside over private dislike, while old villains are drawn back through clever pleas.

sentences.zh: 使大臣果能杜幸門、塞邪徑，則舉錯當而人心服。

translations.literal: If great ministers truly could block the gate of favor and stop the path of evil, then promotion and demotion would be fitting and popular hearts would submit.
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers truly blocked the gate of favor and stopped the path of evil, promotion and demotion would be fitting and popular hearts would submit.

sentences.zh: 臣故曰大臣之心貴乎公。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says the great ministers' hearts value fairness above all.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say great ministers' hearts value fairness above all.

sentences.zh: 台諫平居未嚐立異，遇事不敢盡言。

translations.literal: The censors in ordinary times have never stood apart; when affairs arise they dare not speak to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Censors in ordinary times never stand apart; when affairs arise they dare not speak to the full.

sentences.zh: 有如金人再通，最關國體，近而侍從，下至生徒，莫不力爭，冀裨廟算，獨於言責，不出一辭。

translations.literal: For example, when the Jurchens reopened relations, this most concerned the state's body; from nearby attendants down to students, none did not strive in contention, hoping to aid the temple's plans—only in the duty of speech did they not utter one word.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens reopened relations, a matter most vital to the state, attendants and students alike strove in contention hoping to aid court strategy, yet those charged with speech uttered not one word.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，乾沒巨萬，莫之誰何；

translations.literal: Beneath the imperial carriage hub, embezzlement reached tens of thousands—no one could do anything about it;
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the capital, embezzlement reached vast sums and no one could stop it;

sentences.zh: 州縣之間，罪僅毫髮，摭以塞責。

translations.literal: between prefectures and counties, guilt was only a hair's breadth yet gathered to fill responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: while in prefectures and counties guilt of a hair's breadth was gathered to fill quotas.

sentences.zh: 大臣所欲為之事則遂之，所不右之人則排之。

translations.literal: What great ministers wished to do was carried through; those they did not favor were pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: What great ministers wished to do was carried through; those they did not favor were pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，有宰相奉行台諫風旨之譏，今乃有台諫不敢違中書之誚，豈祖宗設官之初意哉？

translations.literal: In Emperor Renzong's time there was the ridicule that a chief councilor followed the censors' wind and intent; now there is the reproach that censors dare not disobey the Secretariat—how can this be the ancestors' intent in establishing offices?
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Renzong's time people mocked a chief councilor for following censors' wind and intent. Now people mock censors for daring not disobey the Secretariat. How can this be the ancestors' intent in establishing these offices?

sentences.zh: 臣故曰台諫之言貴乎直。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says the censors' words value directness above all.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore say censors' words value directness above all.

sentences.zh: 三者機括所係，願陛下幡然悔悟，昭明德以照臨百官。

translations.literal: These three are where the pivot and trigger lie; your subject wishes Your Majesty suddenly to repent and awaken, make bright virtue shine to oversee the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: These three points hold the pivot of governance. I wish Your Majesty suddenly to repent and awaken, make bright virtue shine, and oversee the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 大臣、台諫，亦宜公心直節，以副望治之意。

translations.literal: Great ministers and censors should also use fair hearts and upright integrity to match the intent of hoping for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers and censors should also use fair hearts and upright integrity to match the hope for good governance.

sentences.zh: 指陳敝事，視前疏尤剴切焉。

translations.literal: Pointing out and presenting defective affairs, it was even more incisive than his former memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In pointing out defective affairs, this memorial was even more incisive than his former one.

sentences.zh: 宓遂請罷，歸。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon requested dismissal and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Mi thereupon requested dismissal and returned home.

sentences.zh: 在告日，擢太府丞，不拜，出知南康軍。

translations.literal: While on leave he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury but did not accept; he went out as prefect of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While on leave he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury but declined the post and was appointed prefect of Nankang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 詣史彌遠別，彌遠曰：“子言甚切當，第愚昧不能行，殊有愧耳。

translations.literal: He went to take leave of Shi Miyuan; Miyuan said: 'Your words are very incisive and fitting, only I am foolish and cannot carry them out—I am deeply ashamed.'
translations.idiomatic: When he went to bid Shi Miyuan farewell, Miyuan said, "Your words are very incisive and fitting, but I am too foolish to carry them out, and I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: ”至官，歲大侵，奏蠲其賦十之九。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, the year suffered great invasion; he memorialized remitting nine-tenths of the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post, a severe famine struck, and he memorialized to remit nine-tenths of the tax levy.

sentences.zh: 會流民群集，宓就役之，築江堤，而給其食。

translations.literal: It happened that displaced people gathered in crowds; Mi put them to labor, built river dikes, and gave them food.
translations.idiomatic: When displaced people gathered in crowds, Mi put them to work building river dikes and provided them with food.

sentences.zh: 時造白鹿洞，與諸生討論。

translations.literal: At the time he built Bailudong and discussed with the various students.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he restored Bailudong Academy and discussed learning with his students.

sentences.zh: 改知南劍州。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Nanjian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Nanjian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時大旱疫，蠲逋賦十數萬，且弛新輸三之一，躬率僚吏持錢粟藥餌戶給之。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought and pestilence; he remitted overdue taxes numbering in the hundreds of thousands, and also relaxed new payments by one-third; he personally led subordinate officials carrying money, grain, and medicine to give household by household.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought and pestilence struck. He remitted overdue taxes numbering in the hundreds of thousands, relaxed new payments by one-third, and personally led officials door to door with money, grain, and medicine.

sentences.zh: 創延平書院，悉仿白鹿洞之規。

translations.literal: He created Yanping Academy, entirely imitating the regulations of Bailudong.
translations.idiomatic: He founded Yanping Academy, entirely following the regulations of Bailudong.

sentences.zh: 知漳州，未行，聞寧宗崩，嗚咽累日。

translations.literal: Appointed prefect of Zhangzhou, before departing he heard Emperor Ningzong had died and sobbed for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Zhangzhou, he had not yet departed when he heard that Emperor Ningzong had died and sobbed for many days.

sentences.zh: 亡何，請致仕。

translations.literal: Before long, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，提點廣東刑獄，章復三上，迄不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing he was made judicial intendant of Guangdong; memorials were submitted three times, yet he never took the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoqing he was appointed judicial intendant of Guangdong, but submitted memorials three times and never took the post.

sentences.zh: 直秘閣，主管崇禧觀，宓拜祠命而辭職名。

translations.literal: Direct Secretariat, in charge of the Chongxi Shrine; Mi accepted the shrine appointment but declined the official title.
translations.idiomatic: He was made direct attendant of the Secretariat with charge of the Chongxi Shrine. Mi accepted the shrine appointment but declined the official title.

sentences.zh: 卒，進職一等致仕。

translations.literal: He died; one rank was advanced for retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted one additional rank in retirement.

sentences.zh: 三學諸生以起宓為請，而沒已閱月矣。

translations.literal: Students of the Three Academies requested Mi's recall, but he had already been dead more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Three Academies petitioned for Mi's recall, but he had already been dead for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 初，宓之在朝也，寺丞丁焴往使金，宓歎曰：“世仇未復，何以好為？

translations.literal: At first, when Mi was at court, Vice Director Ding Huang went as envoy to Jin; Mi sighed and said: 'The age-old foe is not yet restored—how can one act as if all is well?'
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was still at court, Vice Director Ding Huang was sent as envoy to Jin. Mi sighed and said, "Our hereditary enemy is not yet restored. How can we act as if all is well?"

sentences.zh: ”餞詩有“百年中國豈無人”之句。

translations.literal: In his farewell poem there was the line 'For a hundred years has China truly lacked men?'
translations.idiomatic: His farewell poem contained the line, "For a hundred years has China truly lacked men?"

sentences.zh: 後數年，聞關外不靖，以書抵焴曰：“蜀口去關外雖遠，實如一身。

translations.literal: Several years later, hearing the region beyond the passes was unsettled, he sent a letter to Huang saying: 'Shukou is far from beyond the passes, yet in truth it is like one body.'
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, hearing that the region beyond the passes was unsettled, he wrote to Huang: "Shukou is far from beyond the passes, yet in truth they are one body."

sentences.zh: 近事可寒心，皆士大夫之罪，豈非賄道不絕之故耶？

translations.literal: Recent affairs are heart-chilling—all are the crimes of scholar-officials; is it not because the path of bribery never ceases?'
translations.idiomatic: Recent affairs are chilling, and all are the fault of scholar-officials. Is this not because the path of bribery never ceases?"

sentences.zh: ”焴服其言。

translations.literal: Huang submitted to his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huang accepted his argument.

sentences.zh: 宓天性剛毅，信道尤篤，嚐為《朱墨銘》，謂朱屬陽，墨屬陰，以驗理欲分寸之多寡。

translations.literal: Mi's nature was firm and resolute; his faith in the Way was especially deep; he once composed Inscription on Vermilion and Ink, saying vermilion belongs to yang and ink to yin, to test the more or less of principle and desire by minute measure.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was firm and resolute by nature and especially devoted to the Way. He once wrote Inscription on Vermilion and Ink, saying vermilion belongs to yang and ink to yin, using them to measure the balance of principle and desire.

sentences.zh: 自言居官必如顏真卿，居家必如陶潛，而深愛諸葛亮身死家無餘財，庫無餘帛。

translations.literal: He said of himself that in office he must be like Yan Zhenqing, at home like Tao Qian, and deeply loved Zhuge Liang, who at death left his family no surplus wealth and the treasury no surplus cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He said that in office one must be like Yan Zhenqing and at home like Tao Qian, and he deeply admired Zhuge Liang, who at death left his family no surplus wealth and the treasury no surplus cloth.

sentences.zh: 庶乎能蹈其語者，端平初，殿中侍御史王遂首言：“宓事先帝有論諫之直，而不及俟聖化之更，宜褒其身後，以勸天下之為臣者。

translations.literal: Perhaps one could tread his words—in the beginning of Duanping, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Sui first spoke: 'Mi served the late emperor with the directness of remonstrance and discourse, yet did not wait to see the sage transformation renewed; he should be honored after death to encourage all who serve as subjects under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Whether one could truly live by his words is another matter. At the beginning of the Duanping reign, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Sui first said, "Mi served the late emperor with bold remonstrance but did not live to see the sage transformation renewed. He should be honored after death to encourage subjects throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: ”帝為感動，詔贈直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and ordered him posthumously granted direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and ordered him posthumously granted direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《論語注義問答》、《春秋三傳抄》、《讀通鑒綱目》、《唐史贅疣》之稿數十卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: His writings included Questions and Answers on the Meaning of the Analects Commentary, Extracts of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, Reading the Comprehensive Mirror Outlines, and drafts of Excrescences on Tang History in several tens of scrolls, stored in his family.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Questions and Answers on the Meaning of the Analects Commentary, Extracts of the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, Reading the Comprehensive Mirror Outlines, and drafts of Excrescences on Tang History in several tens of scrolls, kept in his family.

sentences.zh: 王霆，字定叟，東陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Ting, style Dingsou, was a native of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ting, whose style was Dingsou, came from Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 高大父豪，帥眾誅方臘，以功補官。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gao led the masses to execute Fang La and received office by merit.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gao led troops to suppress Fang La and received office by merit.

sentences.zh: 霆少有奇氣，試有司不偶，去就武舉，嘉定四年，中絕倫異等。

translations.literal: Ting in youth had unusual spirit; he tested at the civil offices without success, left and took the military examination; in the fourth year of Jiading he passed in the peerless extraordinary grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ting in youth had unusual spirit. He failed the civil examinations, turned to the military examination, and in the fourth year of Jiading passed in the peerless extraordinary grade.

sentences.zh: 喬行簡考藝別頭，喜曰：“吾為朝廷得一帥才矣。

translations.literal: Qiao Xingjian examined his arts as a separate top candidate and said with joy: 'I have obtained a commander talent for the court.'
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian examined his arts as top candidate and said with joy, "I have found a commander for the court."

sentences.zh: 授承節郎，從軍於鄂，帥鍾興嗣戍邊，請於樞密院，以霆為隨軍都錢糧官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of Credentials, followed the army at E, commander Zhong Xingsi garrisoned the frontier, requested from the Bureau of Military Affairs that Ting serve as overall army funds-and-grain officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of Credentials and joined the army at E. Commander Zhong Xingsi, garrisoning the frontier, requested from the Bureau of Military Affairs that Ting serve as the army's overall funds-and-grain officer.

sentences.zh: 總領綦奎委霆專一教閱總效軍，尋委帥師守禦黃州。

translations.literal: Overall director Qi Kui entrusted Ting exclusively to train and review the General Effectiveness Army; soon he was entrusted to command troops defending Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Overall director Qi Kui entrusted Ting exclusively to train the General Effectiveness Army, and soon entrusted him to command troops defending Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 沿江製置副使李辟置幕下，淮右兵叛，遣霆招諭之。

translations.literal: Vice Pacification Commissioner along the river Li recruited him to his staff; Huai West troops rebelled, and he sent Ting to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Pacification Commissioner Li along the Yangzi recruited him to his staff. When Huai West troops rebelled, he sent Ting to summon and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 霆於軍事知無不言，謂：“招募良家子，不可以寅緣關節冒濫其間，防守江麵，全藉正軍，若義勇、民兵，特可為聲援耳。

translations.literal: On military affairs Ting knew nothing he did not speak of, saying: 'Recruiting sons of good families, one cannot through connections and bureaucratic steps let unqualified men slip in among them; defending the river face relies entirely on regular troops—volunteers and militia can only serve as vocal support.'
translations.idiomatic: On military affairs Ting spoke without reserve. He said, "When recruiting sons of good families, one cannot let unqualified men slip in through connections. Defending the Yangzi relies entirely on regular troops; volunteers and militia can serve only as vocal support."

sentences.zh: 而所謂大軍，羸病者多，兵械損舊，豈不敗事。

translations.literal: Yet the so-called great army has many weak and sick, weapons damaged and old—how would this not ruin affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the so-called main army has many weak and sick men and damaged, outdated weapons. How can that not ruin affairs?

sentences.zh: 調兵防江，當於江岸創屋居之，使之專心守禦。

translations.literal: Transferring troops to guard the river, one should create houses on the river bank for them to dwell in, making them concentrate on defense.
translations.idiomatic: Troops transferred to guard the river should be housed on the riverbank so they can concentrate on defense.

sentences.zh: 諸軍伍法既廢，平居則無以稽其虛籍冒請之敝，無以糾其竄逸生事之人，緩急則無以稽其並力向敵之誌，無以連其逃陳不進之心。

translations.literal: Since the various armies' company methods have been abandoned, in ordinary times there is no means to audit the evil of empty registers and false claims, no means to correct those who flee ranks and stir trouble; in urgency or ease there is no means to audit their will to combine strength against the enemy, no means to link their hearts when they flee the line and do not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Since company organization in the armies has been abandoned, in peacetime there is no way to audit empty registers and false claims or correct deserters who stir trouble. In emergencies there is no way to test their will to fight together or bind men who flee the line.

sentences.zh: 此尉繚子所以著束部伍之令，太公謂伍法為要者謂此也。

translations.literal: This is why Master Wei Liao wrote the order binding company organization, and why Grand Duke said company method is essential—he meant this.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Master Wei Liao wrote orders binding company organization, and why the Grand Duke said company method is essential.

sentences.zh: 用兵不以人數多寡為勝負，惟教習之精否，則勝負之形可見矣。

translations.literal: Using troops does not take multitude or fewness of numbers for victory or defeat; only whether training is refined or not—then the form of victory and defeat can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Victory does not depend on numbers but on whether training is refined. Then the outcome can be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 大帥薦之，召試為閣門舍人。

translations.literal: The great commander recommended him; he was summoned and tested as Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The commander recommended him, and he was summoned and tested as Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 入對言：“恢復之說有二：曰規模，曰機會。

translations.literal: Entering audience he said: 'The theory of restoration has two parts: called scale, called opportunity.'
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said, "The theory of restoration has two parts: scale and opportunity."

sentences.zh: 顧今日之規模安在哉？

translations.literal: But where is today's scale?
translations.idiomatic: But where is today's scale?

sentences.zh: 守令所以牧民，而惠養之未加；

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates are for governing the people, yet fostering care is not added;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates exist to govern the people, yet fostering care is not added;

sentences.zh: 將帥所以禦軍，而拊循之未至。

translations.literal: Generals are for controlling armies, yet comforting and guiding has not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Generals exist to command armies, yet comforting and guiding has not arrived.

sentences.zh: 邦財未裕，而楮券之敝浸深；

translations.literal: State finances are not ample, yet the evil of paper notes deepens daily;
translations.idiomatic: State finances are not ample, yet the evil of paper notes deepens daily;

sentences.zh: 軍儲未豐，而和糴之害徒慘。

translations.literal: Military stores are not abundant, yet the harm of harmonized purchase is only cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Military stores are not abundant, yet the harm of harmonized purchase grows only crueler.

sentences.zh: 官有土地而荒蕪，民因賦役而破蕩，獄訟類成冤抑，銓曹率多淹留。

translations.literal: The government has land yet it lies waste; the people because of tax and corvée are broken and scattered; prison cases mostly become wrongful suppression; the selection office mostly has many detained.
translations.idiomatic: Government land lies waste, the people are broken by tax and corvée, prison cases mostly become wrongful suppression, and the selection office mostly detains candidates.

sentences.zh: 薦舉無反坐，貪徒得以引類而通班；

translations.literal: Recommendations have no counter-penalty; greedy fellows can draw their kind and pass into court ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations carry no counter-penalty, so greedy men draw their kind into court ranks;

sentences.zh: 按刺不徇公，微官易以迕意而連譴。

translations.literal: investigations do not follow fairness; petty officials are easily punished in chains for going against intent.
translations.idiomatic: investigations do not follow fairness, and petty officials are easily punished in chains for offending superiors.

sentences.zh: 以言郡計，則紛耗於囊橐包苴；

translations.literal: Speaking of prefectural accounts, they are wasted in purses, bags, and bundles of gifts;
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of prefectural accounts, they are wasted on purses and bundles of gifts;

sentences.zh: 以言戰功，則多私於親昵故舊。

translations.literal: speaking of battle merit, it is mostly private to kin, intimates, and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: speaking of battle merit, it mostly favors kin, intimates, and old friends.

sentences.zh: 至如降卒中處，養虎遺患，輕敵開邊，以肉喂虎。

translations.literal: As for surrendered soldiers placed in the interior, nurturing tigers and leaving calamity; treating the enemy lightly and opening the border—feeding tigers with flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered soldiers are placed in the interior, nurturing tigers and leaving calamity behind; the enemy is treated lightly and the border opened—feeding tigers with flesh.

sentences.zh: 夫以規模之切要者而不滿人意如此，臣敢輕進恢復之說以誤上聽哉？

translations.literal: If what is essential in scale fails to satisfy human intent like this, how dare your subject lightly advance the theory of restoration and mislead what Your Majesty hears?
translations.idiomatic: If what is essential to scale fails to satisfy intent like this, how dare I lightly advance the theory of restoration and mislead Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 凡臣之所陳者，誠播告中外之臣，悉懲其舊而圖其新。

translations.literal: All that your subject has presented truly should be proclaimed to subjects within and without, all punishing the old and plotting the new.
translations.idiomatic: All that I have presented should be proclaimed to subjects within and without, that all may punish the old and plot the new.

sentences.zh: 規模既立，然後義旗一麾，諸道並進，臣力尚壯，願效前驅。

translations.literal: Once scale is established, then the righteous banner is raised once, the various routes advance together; your subject's strength is still robust—I wish to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Once scale is established, then raise the righteous banner once and advance on every route together. My strength is still robust, and I wish to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下堅定而勉圖之。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty be firm and strive to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty be firm and strive to achieve it.

sentences.zh: ”帝稱其言可采。

translations.literal: The emperor said his words could be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said his words could be adopted.

sentences.zh: 升武功大夫，出知濠州，賜金帶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Martial Merit Grand Master, went out as prefect of Haozhou, and was bestowed a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Martial Merit Grand Master, appointed prefect of Haozhou, and bestowed a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 至州，節浮費，糴粟買馬，以備不虞。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture, he cut floating expenses, purchased grain and bought horses to prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the prefecture, he cut unnecessary expenses, purchased grain and horses, and prepared against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 尋差知安豐軍，臣僚上言：“王霆在濠，人甚安之，不宜輕易。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned to govern Anfeng Commandery; court officials memorialized: 'Wang Ting is at Hao; the people are very settled there—he should not be lightly moved.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to govern Anfeng Commandery. Court officials memorialized, "Wang Ting is at Hao and the people are very settled there. He should not be lightly moved."

sentences.zh: ”詔再任濠，職事修舉，特轉橫班。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to serve again at Hao; his duties were well carried out, and he was specially transferred to the lateral rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to serve again at Hao. His duties were well carried out, and he was specially transferred to the lateral rank.

sentences.zh: 諸使交薦之。

translations.literal: Various commissioners repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Various commissioners repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 北兵至浮光，其民奔遁，相屬於道，朝論以為霆可守之，乃知光州兼沿邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Northern troops reached Fuguang; its people fled in panic, following one another on the road; court opinion held that Ting could defend it, and he was made prefect of Guang Prefecture while also serving as frontier overall patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops reached Fuguang and its people fled in panic along the roads. Court opinion held that Ting could defend the region, and he was made prefect of Guang Prefecture while also serving as frontier overall patrol commissioner.

sentences.zh: 冒雪夜行，倍道疾馳至州，分遣間探，整飭戰守之具，大戰於謝令橋，光人遂安。

translations.literal: Braving snow he traveled by night, doubled the road and galloped swiftly to the prefecture, sent out scouts in divisions, put battle and defense equipment in order, fought a great battle at Xieling Bridge, and the people of Guang were then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Braving snow he traveled by night and raced to the prefecture at double speed. He sent out scouts, put battle equipment in order, fought a great battle at Xieling Bridge, and the people of Guang were secured.

sentences.zh: 督府魏了翁以書來慰安之，以緡錢十萬勞其軍。

translations.literal: Supervisor Wei Liaoweng sent a letter to comfort him and gave one hundred thousand strings to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Wei Liaoweng sent a letter to comfort him and gave one hundred thousand strings to reward his army.

sentences.zh: 霆以召，尋為吉州刺史，仍知光州。

translations.literal: Ting was summoned; soon he was made prefect of Ji Prefecture while still governing Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was summoned to court and soon made prefect of Ji Prefecture while still governing Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 霆固辭，丞相鄭清之、製置使史嵩之皆數以書留霆，霆不從，且曰：“士大夫當以世從道，不可以道從世也。

translations.literal: Ting firmly declined; Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Shi Songzhi several times sent letters to detain Ting; Ting would not follow, and said: 'Scholar-officials should let the age follow the Way, not let the Way follow the age.'
translations.idiomatic: Ting firmly declined. Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Shi Songzhi repeatedly wrote to detain him, but Ting would not comply and said, "Scholar-officials should let the age follow the Way, not let the Way follow the age."

sentences.zh: 再授閣門舍人，尋為達州刺史、右屯衛大將軍兼知蘄州，不赴。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Gate Attendant; soon he was made prefect of Da Prefecture and Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard while also governing Qizhou—but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Gate Attendant, then made prefect of Da Prefecture and Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard while also governing Qizhou, but did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋遷淮西馬步軍副總管兼淮西遊擊軍副都統製。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to vice overall commander of Huai West horse and foot armies while also vice overall controller of Huai West mobile armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice overall commander of Huai West horse and foot armies and vice overall controller of Huai West mobile armies.

sentences.zh: 論遊擊軍十事，不報。

translations.literal: He discussed ten matters concerning the mobile army; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed ten matters concerning the mobile army, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was made intendant of the Chongxi Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of the Chongxi Shrine.

sentences.zh: 知高郵軍，流民邦傑聚眾三千人為盜，霆剿其渠魁，餘黨悉散。

translations.literal: Governing Gaoyou Commandery, the displaced person Bang Jie gathered a crowd of three thousand as bandits; Ting suppressed the ringleaders and the rest scattered entirely.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Gaoyou Commandery, he suppressed a band of three thousand displaced people led by Bang Jie; the ringleaders were killed and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 時議出師，和者甚多，霆以為：“莫若遣間探覘敵情，如不得已然後行之；

translations.literal: At the time expedition was debated and many favored peace; Ting considered: 'Better to send scouts to observe enemy conditions; if there is no other way, then act;'
translations.idiomatic: At the time expedition was debated and many favored it. Ting argued, "Better to send scouts to observe enemy conditions, and act only if there is no other way;

sentences.zh: 否則無故自蕩其根本，是外兵未至而內兵先慘烈也。

translations.literal: otherwise without cause one shakes one's own foundation—this is outer troops not yet arrived while inner troops first suffer bitter slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the court will shake its own foundation without cause, and inner troops will suffer bitter slaughter before outer enemies even arrive."

sentences.zh: ”諸軍畢行，惟高郵遲之，境內賴以安全。

translations.literal: All armies fully marched; only Gaoyou delayed, and within the borders they relied on this for safety.
translations.idiomatic: All armies marched, but Gaoyou delayed, and the region relied on that delay for safety.

sentences.zh: 由是與時迕，而讒者益眾。

translations.literal: Because of this he went against the times, and slanderers grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he went against the times, and slanderers grew more numerous.

sentences.zh: 提舉雲台觀。

translations.literal: He was made intendant of the Yuntai Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of the Yuntai Shrine.

sentences.zh: 執政期論邊事，且謂朝廷即有齊安之命。

translations.literal: The councilors scheduled discussion of frontier affairs and said the court would soon have the Qian'an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The councilors scheduled discussion of frontier affairs and said the court would soon appoint him to Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 霆曰：“秋防已急，邊守不宜臨時更易，盍少需之。

translations.literal: Ting said: 'Autumn defense is already urgent; frontier defenders should not be changed at the last moment—why not wait a little?'
translations.idiomatic: Ting said, "Autumn defense is already urgent. Frontier defenders should not be changed at the last moment. Why not wait a little?"

sentences.zh: ”乃授帶行左領軍衛大將軍，充沿江製置副使司計議官，霆乃撰《沿江等邊志》一編上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Grand General of the Left Army Guard with belt, serving as planning officer of the Vice Pacification Commission along the river; Ting then compiled one fascicle of Records of Frontier Regions along the River and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand General of the Left Army Guard with belt and planning officer of the Vice Pacification Commission along the Yangzi. Ting compiled Records of Frontier Regions along the River and presented it.

sentences.zh: 製置使董槐、鄧泳交薦之，差知壽昌軍，改蘄州，建學舍，祠忠臣。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioners Dong Huai and Deng Yong repeatedly recommended him; he was assigned to govern Shouchang Commandery, changed to Qizhou, built a school hall, and enshrined loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioners Dong Huai and Deng Yong repeatedly recommended him. He was assigned to govern Shouchang Commandery, transferred to Qizhou, built a school hall, and enshrined loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 嚐歎曰：“兩淮藩籬也，大江門戶也，三輔堂奧也。

translations.literal: He once sighed and said: 'The Two Huai are the fence; the Great River is the gate; the Three Metropolises are the inner hall.'
translations.idiomatic: He once sighed and said, "The Two Huai are the fence, the Great River is the gate, and the Three Metropolises are the inner hall."

sentences.zh: 藩籬不固則門戶且危，門戶既危則堂奧豈能久安乎？

translations.literal: If the fence is not secure, then the gate will soon be in peril; if the gate is already in peril, how can the inner hall long be secure?
translations.idiomatic: If the fence is not secure, the gate will soon be in peril. If the gate is in peril, how can the inner hall long remain secure?

sentences.zh: ”於是貽書丞相杜範，乞瞰江審察形勢，置三新城：蘄春置於龍眼磯，安慶置於孟城，滁陽置於宣化。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent a letter to Chief Councilor Du Fan, begging to overlook the river and examine the posture of force, establishing three new cities: Qichun at Longyan Jetty, Anqing at Mengcheng, Chuyang at Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Chief Councilor Du Fan, asking to survey the Yangzi and examine the strategic situation, and establish three new cities: Qichun at Longyan Jetty, Anqing at Mengcheng, and Chuyang at Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 初，其父析業，霆獨以讓其兄。

translations.literal: At first, when his father divided the estate, Ting alone yielded to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When his father divided the family estate, Ting alone yielded his share to his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 處宗族有恩意，嚐訓其子弟曰：“窮理盡性，學之本也。

translations.literal: In dealing with the clan he had kindness and intent; he once instructed his sons and nephews: 'Exhausting principle and fulfilling nature—this is the root of learning.'
translations.idiomatic: He treated his clan with kindness and once instructed his sons and nephews, "Exhausting principle and fulfilling nature is the root of learning."

sentences.zh: ”有《玉溪集》行於世。

translations.literal: He had Jade Stream Collected Works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Jade Stream Collected Works circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：吳昌裔訪道東南，一何勤哉！

translations.literal: The discussion says: Wu Changyi sought the Way in the southeast—how diligent!
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Wu Changyi sought the Way in the southeast—how diligent he was!

sentences.zh: 故其造深醇，見諸事功者，足以知其學無雜也。

translations.literal: Therefore his achievement was deep and pure; what appears in practical accomplishments suffices to know his learning had no admixture.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement was deep and pure, and what appears in his practical accomplishments shows that his learning had no admixture.

sentences.zh: 汪綱之遺愛在越，先民所謂擇賢久任者，固不我欺矣。

translations.literal: Wang Gang's lingering love was in Yue; what the ancients called choosing the worthy and employing them long—the ancients truly did not deceive us.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gang's lingering benevolence was in Yue. What the ancients called choosing the worthy and employing them long—the ancients did not deceive us.

sentences.zh: 陳宓以宰相子，論諫之直，於今有光。

translations.literal: Chen Mi, as a chief councilor's son, had the directness of discourse and remonstrance that still shines today.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mi, though a chief councilor's son, had a remonstrance so direct that it still shines today.

sentences.zh: 王霆通兵家言，而謂不可以道從世，此古人謀帥貴乎“說《禮》、《樂》而敦《詩》、《書》”也。

translations.literal: Wang Ting mastered the military family's words, yet said one cannot let the Way follow the age—this is what the ancients meant in seeking commanders, valuing those who 'discuss Rites and Music and cherish the Odes and Documents.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ting mastered military theory yet said one cannot let the Way follow the age. This is what the ancients meant in seeking commanders who "discuss Rites and Music and cherish the Odes and Documents."
